guide.title: Mei's Overview
guide.text:
Mei is a Tank who relies on various types of
crowd control to mess up the enemy plans
and some peculiar forms of self-sustain
to survive longer during team fights.

guide.title: Mei's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
High survivability
Decent damage output
Versatile crowd control
Good mobility
Weaknesses
Not able to peel from high mobility Heroes (like Tracer)
Weak to Knockbacks and Roots

guide.title: Mei's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Mei synergizes with
Considering that her Basic Abilities are not that reliable
when trying to engage enemy Heroes,
Mei prefers having allied Heroes who can initiate for her (for example Maiev),
so that she can follow-up with Blizzard.
Similarly, Mei benefits from Heroes that can help her
to keep enemy Heroes within Blizzard
by creating impassable terrain (like Tassadar with Force Wall)
or by Knocking back enemy Heroes nearby
(such as Maiev with Umbral Bind).
As she provides a lot of crowd control,
Mei performs better with Heroes that can follow-up
her Abilities with burst damage (for example Jaina).
Mei's high Slow uptime is good for
allied Heroes who get increased damage from it (such as Ace In The Hole
at Level 1 on Raynor) as the condition for triggering
their increased damage will easily be met.
Mei is countered by
Mei suffers while facing Heroes who have access to any kind of
mobility because she will have a hard time trying
to engage and her peeling tools
will not accomplish anything (for example Tracer).
Roots (such as Entangling Roots by Malfurion)
and Knockbacks (like Face Melt by E.T.C.)
can stop her while trying to engage with Icing.
While she does not gets completely shut down by them,
Mei also does not like effects that reduce healing (for example
Biotic Grenade by Ana), deal
percent-based damage (such as Cursed Bullet
at Level 10 by Greymane), or deal bonus damage to Shields
(like EMP Grenade at Level 13 by Lt. Morales).
The same is true for Heroes who can poke her team
from a long distance (such as Li-Ming).
Last but not the least, you can combine crowd control
and burst damage to kill Mei before she can even use
Cryo-Freeze defensively.

guide.text:

Mei's weaker maps
Mei does better on Maps where the fights happen on a small Capture Point
(like Braxis Holdout), that have narrow passages where she can get
more value from her kit (for example Cursed Hollow),
and that have a Boss Camp that goes in lane once captured.
When picking Ice Storm at Level 1,
Mei has good waveclear, making her a good pick
on Maps where macro is important. Keep in mind, though,
that she will not be able to help you capture Mercenary Camps quickly.

guide.title: Mei's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
The moderate Slow provided by Snow Blind can be used to slightly increase the chance that Blizzard will connect and that Icing will hit enemy Heroes from a good angle.
The high but decaying Slow provided by Icing must be used to drastically increase the chance that the Stun at the end of Blizzard will trigger.
Avalanche can split the enemy team by pushing some enemy Heroes away, even behind impassable terrain.
After you aggressively get behind an enemy Hero by using Icing, you can push them towards your team with Avalanche.
If you catch 3 enemy Heroes with Avalanche, you can follow the snowball with Icing to be in range for casting Blizzard as a follow-up to the prolonged Stun.
Ice Wall can be used to split the enemy team by putting in Time Stop some Heroes and fighting the others.
A well-timed Blizzard—exactly 0.5 seconds after your Heroic Ability connects—will always Stun enemy Heroes affected by Ice Wall.
You can use Ice Wall behind enemy Heroes to block their retreat or in front of them to stop their engage.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Mei's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Mei is a Tank that excels at punishing enemy Heroes who
lack mobility to play around her Slows.
She has access to powerful Heroic Abilities that, when having a Mage
in team, can be used to make scary combos.
That said, Avalanche and Ice Wall
are already strong on their own, both for engaging
and for peeling. With a bit of creativity, you can make
powerful tricks with them.

abilities.title: Mei's Tips and Tricks
abilities.text:
The moderate Slow provided by Snow Blind can be used to slightly increase the chance that Blizzard will connect and that Icing will hit enemy Heroes from a good angle.
The high but decaying Slow provided by Icing must be used to drastically increase the chance that the Stun at the end of Blizzard will trigger.
Avalanche can split the enemy team by pushing some enemy Heroes away, even behind impassable terrain.
After you aggressively get behind an enemy Hero by using Icing, you can push them towards your team with Avalanche.
If you catch 3 enemy Heroes with Avalanche, you can follow the snowball with Icing to be in range for casting Blizzard as a follow-up to the prolonged Stun.
Ice Wall can be used to split the enemy team by putting in Time Stop some Heroes and fighting the others.
A well-timed Blizzard—exactly 0.5 seconds after your Heroic Ability connects—will always Stun enemy Heroes affected by Ice Wall.
You can use Ice Wall behind enemy Heroes to block their retreat or in front of them to stop their engage.

abilities.title: Snow Blind
abilities.text:
Snow Blind
(Q)
Mei
Mana: 35
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Throw a snowball that hits all enemies in an area. Enemies hit take 70 (+4% per level) damage, are Slowed by 35%, and are Blinded for 1.75 seconds.
Snow Blind is a Basic Ability that deals damage,
Slows, and Blinds all enemies in
a small target area.
You can use this Ability to peel your team or even to
Slow an enemy Hero that you want to engage
on, so that you will have more chances to Knockback
them in the desired direction when Icing ends.

abilities.title: Blizzard
abilities.text:
Blizzard
(W)
Mei
Mana: 70
Cooldown: 14 seconds
Command Snowball to create a Blizzard at the target location for 2 seconds. Enemies within the blizzard take 13 (+4% per level) damage every 0.25 seconds and are Slowed by 7%, stacking up to 35%. When the Blizzard ends, enemies within its area take an additional 75 (+4% per level) damage and are Stunned for 1.25 seconds.
Blizzard is a Basic Ability that deals damage and applies
a stacking Slow to enemies in a big target area over 2 seconds;
furthermore, it deals additional damage and Stuns when it ends.
Considering the 2-second delay before the Stun effect goes off,
you should usually start your engage with Snow Blind
to Slow enemy Heroes inside the Blizzard
and then follow-up with Icing
to Knock them back if they try to leave.
In total, this Ability will deal 192 damage to all enemies hit, making it a
decent tool for clearing Minions in some scenarios. That said, if your team
does not lack waveclear, you better keep it for other uses.

abilities.title: Icing
abilities.text:
Icing
(E)
Mei
Mana: 70
Cooldown: 14 seconds
Slide quickly in the targeted direction. When this effect ends, enemies near Mei are knocked back, take 52 (+4% per level) damage, and are Slowed by 80%, rapidly decaying over 1.5 seconds.
Can be canceled during sliding.
Icing is a Basic Ability that gives mobility,
mostly useful for engaging or escaping. At the end of the slide,
Mei will Knockback, deal damage, and apply a decaying
Slow to all enemies within range.
The slide can be manually canceled by pressing the same key again, a feature
that is extremely useful to better Knockback enemy Heroes into a previously cast
Blizzard and increase the chances they will be
Stunned at its end. Alternatively, you can cast Blizzard on
top of the decaying Slow provided at the end of Icing to get a similar result.
Considering that many of your Abilities have a delay,
you can use the Slow provided by Icing
to increase the chances that they will connect on the desired enemy Heroes.
This trick is especially useful for landing your Heroic Abilities
because they have a long cooldown and therefore it is important to avoid wasting them.
Due to its high Mana cost and low damage, we recommend to avoid using it for
clearing Minions, especially because the Knockback will
spread them all and the rest of your team will spend more time to clear them.

abilities.title: Avalanche
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Avalanche
(R)
Mei
Heroic
Mana: 80
Cooldown: 90 seconds
After 0.5 seconds, roll a massive snowball that consumes enemy Heroes in its path. At the end of its path, the snowball crumbles, releasing the consumed Heroes, dealing 220 (+4% per level) damage and Stunning them for 0.5 seconds per Hero consumed.
Avalanche is a Heroic Ability that, after a short delay,
puts every enemy Hero hit in Stasis while the snowball is
rolling and then Stuns them when it breaks at the end.

Stasis does not work on Unstoppable enemy Heroes,
so it will just pierce through them (for example Deathwing).
It is important to know that the snowball will go through impassable
terrain—including the terrain covered by Structures—however,
if the ending point happens to be impassable terrain, then the snowball will
break pre-emptively. While it is not that important to predict that in the
middle of the Map, it is obvious and therefore easy to remember that it will
always happen when the snowball reaches the external border of the Map.
Even if you can cast this Heroic Ability to push enemy Heroes out of position,
it can be occasionally better to push the rest of their team away instead.

abilities.title: Ice Wall
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Ice Wall
(R)
Mei
Heroic
Mana: 50
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Vector Targeting
After a 0.75 second delay, create an impassable wall that traps enemy Heroes hit for 2.5 seconds. When the wall expires, trapped Heroes are Slowed by 75%, decaying over 3 seconds.
Ice Wall is a Heroic Ability that, after a short delay,
puts every enemy Hero hit in Time Stop for a few seconds
and then applies a decaying Slow.
Remember that the wall counts as impassable terrain,
blocking the path to both allies and enemies.
It is worth mentioning that Time Stop affects Unstoppable
enemies too, freezing them for a while but not removing the Unstoppable from them,
unless the Unstoppable is on the ground (such as Sanctification
by Tyrael) and will eventually expire.
You can use this Ability in various ways: from engaging
to peeling, from isolating some Heroes to fight their allies
to blocking them all in place for a wombo-combo.
If you cast Blizzard 0.5 seconds after the
Time Stop effect starts, you will Stun
all enemy Heroes affected by it.
In case you want to use Blizzard before Ice Wall,
keep in mind that the Time Stop will not cancel the Stun, but it will keep going
after the Time Stop ends.
Avoid using this Heroic Ability on enemy Heroes
who are going to be hit by the final effect of Blizzard or any other impactful
Ability cast by allied Heroes (for example Pyroblast
by Kael'thas) because the Time Stop will make them completely immune
for the duration.
Keep in mind that this Heroic Ability has Vector Targeting: press the key,
drag the mouse in the desired direction, and release the key.

abilities.title: Cryo-Freeze
abilities.text:
Cryo-Freeze
(D)
Mei
Cooldown: 40 seconds
Become encased in ice for 3 seconds, gaining a rapidly decaying Shield that absorbs up to 1104 (+4% per level) damage. While active, this Shield grants Unstoppable and restores up to 35% of Mei's maximum Health.
Cryo-Freeze is a Trait that drastically increases
Mei's survivability by giving her a powerful Shield for 3 seconds that heals her
and makes her Unstoppable, but she cannot move for
the duration. If needed, you can choose to cancel the effect pre-emptively
by pressing the same key again.

(Level 7)
Mei
Blizzard reduces the damage dealt by enemy Heroes inside of its area by 40%.
When Blizzard ends, enemy Heroes still within its area gain this effect for an additional 4 seconds.
Induce Hibernation is a weak Talent that reduces the
damage done by enemy Heroes inside the area covered by Blizzard.
If they do not get out before Blizzard ends, they will keep the same debuff
for a few more seconds, even if Blizzard and its Stun will be over at that point.
That said, we do not recommend this Talent because the crowd control
provided by Blizzard is enough to indirectly reduce incoming damage.
Induce Hibernation has synergy with Flurry and Cooling Servos
at Level 13 because they can both reduces Blizzard's cooldown and make you benefit
from this Talent more often.
✔
Skating Away
(Level 7)
Mei
When Icing ends, Mei and all nearby allied Heroes gain 20% Movement Speed and 50 Physical Armor for 3 seconds.
Skating Away is a strong Talent that, when you cast
Icing, gives Mei and nearby allied Heroes a good amount of
Movement Speed and Physical Armor for a few seconds.
The additional Movement Speed may help you body block
enemy Heroes, especially if they are affected by one of your Slows,
and nearby allied Heroes to reposition either offensively or defensively.
The bonus Physical Armor makes Mei more resistant immediately after
engaging and increases the survivability of nearby
allied Heroes as well.
Skating Away has synergy with Cold Front
and Cooling Servos because they can both reduce Icing's cooldown
and make you benefit from this Talent more often.
?
Backup Battery
(Level 7)
Mei
Cooldown: 70 seconds
Activate to remove all Roots and Slows and regenerate 20% of maximum Health over 2 seconds. The cooldown of this ability is reduced by 10 seconds each time Mei picks up a Regeneration Globe.
Backup Battery is a situational Talent that increases
Mei's survivability by providing her an Active Ability to remove Roots
and Slows from herself and/or to heal for a considerable amount
when doing so.
While it has a relatively long cooldown, picking up
Regeneration Globes will shorten it. You can activate it at any moment,
even if you have full Health.

talent_pages.title: Level 10 Talents for Mei
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
?
Avalanche
(Level 10)
Mei
Mana: 80
Cooldown: 90 seconds
After 0.5 seconds, roll a massive snowball that consumes enemy Heroes in its path. At the end of its path, the snowball crumbles, releasing the consumed Heroes, dealing 220 (+4% per level) damage and Stunning them for 0.5 seconds per Hero consumed.
Avalanche is a decent Heroic Ability for splitting the
enemy team and immediately starting a team fight to abuse the numerical advantage.
Avalanche has synergy with Acclimation at Level 16 because
it can increase any damage dealt by up to 20%.
✔
Ice Wall
(Level 10)
Mei
Mana: 50
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Vector Targeting
After a 0.75 second delay, create an impassable wall that traps enemy Heroes hit for 2.5 seconds. When the wall expires, trapped Heroes are Slowed by 75%, decaying over 3 seconds.
Ice Wall is a strong Heroic Ability that makes up for
Mei's mediocre engage by giving her a powerful tool that
can be used to setup enemy Heroes for your team and/or split the enemy team.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Mei
talent_pages.text:
✔
Flurry
(Level 13)
Mei
While in her own Blizzard, Mei gains 50% increased Attack Speed and Blizzard's cooldown refreshes 125% faster. If Mei is in her own Blizzard when it ends, gain these bonuses for 3 additional seconds.
Flurry is a strong Talent that gives Mei bonus Attack Speed
and makes Blizzard refresh its cooldown faster
while she is within its area and for 3 second after being "hit" by its ending part.
The bonus Attack Speed has decent synergy with Heat Transfer
at Level 1 because it allows you to get more value from
the bonus Attack Damage while the cooldown reduction has strong synergy with
Cold Front at Level 4 because it basically aligns
Blizzard's cooldown with Icing's cooldown.
?
Cooling Servos
(Level 13)
Mei
While Cryo-Freeze is active, Mei's Basic Ability cooldowns recover 200% faster.
Passive: Basic Attacks Slow by 20% for 1.5 seconds.
Cooling Servos is a good Talent that makes every
Mei's Basic Attack apply a small Slow to the target
and makes Cryo-Freeze heavily increase the cooldown
refresh rate of every Basic Ability.
The bonus Slow has synergy with
Heat Transfer at Level 1 in prolonged team fights because
that Talent requires the target to be Slowed and your Basic Abilities
will not always be available to give you that.
The cooldown reduction provided
is extremely helpful to disengage when in danger,
but it can also be used aggressively to keep the fight going when not risky.
Cooling Servos has strong synergy with Crystallize at Level 4
because standing still for the whole duration of Cryo-Freeze
is often dangerous without the Spell Armor provided by it.
?
Polar Vortex
(Level 13)
Mei
Using an ability causes Mei to deal 24 (+4% per level) damage a second to nearby enemies for 4 seconds. Enemy Heroes damaged by this effect also have their Movement Speed and Attack Speed Slowed by 20%.
Polar Vortex is a good Talent that makes Mei deal
area of effect damage to nearby enemies for a few seconds
after casting an Ability.
In addition to being damaged, enemy Heroes will have
their Attack Speed reduced and a Slow applied to them.
Slows help you to body-block
and to connect Blizzard.
The bonus Slow has synergy with Heat Transfer
at Level 1 in short team fights because that Talent requires
the target to be Slowed.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Mei
talent_pages.text:
?
Fresh Powder
(Level 16)
Mei
Snow Blind gains an additional charge and its range is increased by 33%.
Fresh Powder is a situational Talent that provides a second
charge of Snow Blind and slightly
increases its range.
The second charge allows you to Blind
enemy Heroes twice in a row and has synergy with all
Snow Blind-related Talents: Heavy Pack at Level 1,
Slushball at Level 4, and The Big One at Level 20.
✔
Black Ice
(Level 16)
Mei
Icing's Slow effect no longer decays over its duration. Icing deals 300% more damage to enemies very close to Mei.
Black Ice is a strong Talent that turns the decaying
Slow provided by Icing into a powerful
non-decaying Slow and increases the damage done by Icing to very close enemies as well.
The buff to the Slow helps the final part of Blizzard to
connect and therefore increases the chance that the Stun
will happen.
The bonus damage helps your team secure kills before the
focused enemy Hero can be saved, but be careful not to
mess up your team's follow-up with
Icing's knockback effect.
?
Acclimation
(Level 16)
Mei
Each time Mei Stuns or Slows an enemy Hero, the damage she deals and healing she receives is increased by 1%, stacking up to 20 times. While at maximum stacks, Mei also gains 10 Armor. Lasts 8 seconds.
Acclimation is a good Talent that increases Mei's
survivability in prolonged team fights. In particular, it gives Mei increased
healing from any source (notably her Cryo-Freeze) and a bit of Armor.
Keep in mind that the bonus starts low and gradually increase while fighting,
so we cannot really consider it a good anti-burst tool;
instead, see it as a tool to increase your sustain, especially when your team
has a sustain Healer rather than a burst one.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Mei
talent_pages.text:
?
Cascade
(Level 20)
Mei
While traveling, Avalanche constantly launches a volley of untalented Snow Blind snowballs ahead of itself.
Passive: Reduce the cooldown of Avalanche by 30 seconds.
Cascade is a good Talent that reduces the cooldown of
Avalanche and makes it launch 22 untalented Snow Blind
projectiles: 17 shots while rolling, and 5 shots at the end.
While the Heroes inside Avalanche cannot be hit by anything, the first group
of shots can hit enemy Heroes before they get caught by it. Both groups of shots
will hit a single Hero with 1-4 shots that will deal between 70 and 280 damage in total,
randomly increasing the damage of Avalanche from 220 to 780 damage, but averaging 500 damage.
✔
Shatter
(Level 20)
Mei
When Ice Wall expires, trapped enemy Heroes hit take 210 (+4% per level) damage and have their Armor reduced by 25 for 5 seconds.
Shatter is a strong Talent that turns the already powerful
Ice Wall into a scary engage tool by
dealing damage and reducing the Armor of all enemy Heroes caught.
✘
The Big One
(Level 20)
Mei
Every 15 seconds, the next Snow Blind you cast has 67% increased area and 200% increased damage.
The Big One is a weak Talent that increases the
damage done and the area covered by Snow Blind, but not every
time you cast it because there is an internal cooldown of 15 seconds.
You cannot use Cooling Servos at Level 13 to reduce its cooldown,
but you can use Slushball at Level 4 to disable 2 adjacent Towers.
The internal cooldown
removes the otherwise possible synergy with cooldown-reducing Talents:
Heavy Pack at Level 1, Cooling Servos
at Level 13, and Fresh Powder at Level 16.
We do not recommend this Talent because it does not provide
enough value compared to the other options in the same Tier.
?
Flash Freeze
(Level 20)
Mei
When Mei takes fatal damage she instantly gains Cryo-Freeze. This effect has a 180 second cooldown.
Flash Freeze is a situational Talent that considerably increases
Mei's survivability when she is going to die, but only once every 3 minutes.
The automatic activation allows her to survive against scary
engages based on crowd-control
paired with burst damage, a combination that would otherwise
not give you enough time to manually activate Cryo-Freeze.
Cryo-Freeze and Flash Freeze do not share their cooldowns,
so you can use them one after another, regardless of the order.
If you are scared of enemy crowd control effects,
prefer using Cryo-Freeze first because Flash Freeze will automatically go off
when you are not able to cast your Abilities.
